cards.explanation: The reason the writer gives is so the bodies would not stay up on the Sabbath. The next day was a High Sabbath, so the Jews asked Pilate, the Roman governor, to have the legs broken and the bodies taken down. The text says the point was that the bodies would not remain on the cross during the Sabbath.
The answer is False. John 19:32 says the soldiers broke the legs of the first man who had been crucified with Jesus, and those of the other. So both men got the same treatment, friends.

The answer is no, they did not break His legs, because He was already dead. When the soldiers came to Jesus, they saw that He was already dead, so they did not break His legs. The writer gives that exact reason in the verse. Sometimes the text just hands you the answer, and I take those.

He tells it so readers will believe too. The writer says the one who saw it knows he is telling the truth, so that you also may believe. Notice the 'you' there, friends. The writer is talking straight to whoever is reading.

The answer is True. The writer says these things happened so that the Scripture would be fulfilled, and then he quotes: “Not one of His bones will be broken.” That's the soldiers not breaking Jesus' legs. He wants us to see the Scripture and the cross lining up.

The answer is that people will look on Him. The writer says another Scripture says, “They will look on the One they have pierced.” The prophet Zechariah wrote those words (Zechariah 12:10). The spear in this passage is why the writer brings it up.

The answer is the Jews. John 19:38 says Joseph of Arimathea was a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews. That's the text's own reason. Keeping a secret is hard work, friends, and I should know, because I once hid a burnt batch under a dish towel.
The answer is False. Joseph of Arimathea asked Pilate, and Pilate gave him permission. Then Joseph came and removed the body of Jesus. I bet asking took some nerve, friends, but the answer was yes.

The spices were used to wrap the body for burial. The text says they took the body of Jesus and wrapped it in linen cloths with the spices. Nicodemus, a Pharisee who had come to Jesus at night (John 3:1-2), brought the myrrh and aloes. It was a burial, and the spices went with the cloths.

The answer is True. John 19:40 says they wrapped the body in linen cloths with the spices, according to the Jewish burial custom. The writer tells us they did it the way it was done, friends. It was careful work.

What's in the garden is a new tomb where no one had been laid. John 19:41 says that in the garden was a new tomb in which no one had yet been laid. Nobody had used it before. That's the tomb the writer points to.

They laid Him there because it was the day of Preparation and the tomb was nearby. John 19:42 says they placed Jesus there because it was the Jewish day of Preparation and the tomb was nearby. Those are the two reasons the text gives. Sometimes the best place is the one that's close.
